rules.text: Every public function must carry a docstring.
Validation belongs in src/auth/; nothing else may define it.
Every change must be reviewed by a second engineer.
rules.reason: the map carries no evidence about review process

findings.title: Session setup repeated across two flows, two ways
findings.rationale: load_user runs, a token step follows, and audit_login closes, in both user_login and password_reset. Two chains share those endpoints and differ only in the token step, so they are reported once.
findings.suggestion: Extract the shared endpoints into one begin_session helper that takes the token step.

findings.title: Email validation implemented in 3 places
findings.rationale: Three functions independently validate email format with equivalent logic.

sites.snippet:
def check_email(raw):
    return EMAIL_PATTERN.fullmatch(raw) is not None

def is_valid_email(s):
    return re.match(r'[^@]+@[^@]+', s) is not None

findings.suggestion: Consolidate into one helper and have the other two call it.

findings.title: src/auth/session.py exports 9 functions and no caller uses more than 2
findings.rationale: Nine exported functions, six consumer files, and the widest consumer calls two of them. One interface is standing where its callers want several: the request-side lookups and the audit writers have no consumer in common.
findings.suggestion: Split the module along the two groups its callers already use.

findings.title: session, schemas and validators call each other in a ring
findings.rationale: Three files across two top-level packages depend on each other in a cycle, so none of them can be read, tested or changed on its own.
findings.suggestion: Invert the validators-to-session edge behind an interface the session module implements, so the dependency points one way.

findings.title: Tests reach past src/auth/session.py's interface into 3 internals
findings.rationale: Two test functions call _decode_cookie, _rotate_key and _write_audit_row directly, and the module exports nine functions, so there was an interface to test through. `exported` is the map's per-language heuristic and defaults to true where the convention is unclear, so this under-reports rather than over-reports.
findings.suggestion: Exercise the three through load_user and refresh_token, so the module stays free to change how it decodes and rotates.

findings.title: Validation defined outside src/auth/ in 2 places
findings.rationale: R-02 confines validation to src/auth/. Two catalogued functions define it elsewhere.
findings.rule: Validation belongs in src/auth/; nothing else may define it.

sites.snippet:
def check_email(raw):
    return EMAIL_PATTERN.fullmatch(raw) is not None

def is_valid_email(s):
    return re.match(r'[^@]+@[^@]+', s) is not None

findings.suggestion: Move both into src/auth/validators.py and import them where they are used.

findings.title: handle_request has a fan-out of 11
findings.rationale: handle_request calls 11 functions directly, above the fan-out threshold of 8.
findings.suggestion: Group the validation, persistence and notification calls into three helpers.

findings.title: export_view selects among 3 renderers with a conditional chain
findings.rationale: render_pdf, render_html and render_csv share a name shape and a signature, and export_view picks between them with an if/elif on a format string, so adding a fourth format means editing export_view. Confirmed by reading the selection: a lookup table, a registry or a polymorphic call here would not have been a finding.
findings.suggestion: Register the three renderers by format key and have export_view look one up.

findings.title: src/web/views.py reaches into 7 other modules
findings.rationale: Its functions call into seven distinct files and four call in. This is a proxy for more than one reason to change rather than a proof of one: the module graph shows the spread, not the intent behind it.
findings.suggestion: Give the persistence and notification calls their own module, so views depends on two collaborators instead of seven.

findings.title: 2 pass-through functions in src/api/schemas.py
findings.rationale: Each takes the same parameters as the single function it calls and does nothing else, so it adds a name a caller must learn and hides no work.
findings.suggestion: Have the two callers reach session.decode and session.encode directly.

findings.title: ReadOnlyStore.write raises where its siblings return
findings.rationale: The map stated the family: all three stores carry overrides naming Store.write, so no name matching was involved. Verification confirmed the two counts left — dispatch_write holds one through the Store type, and only this member refuses; FileStore.write and MemoryStore.write both return, so a caller holding a Store cannot rely on write working.

sites.snippet:
def write(self, key, value):
    raise NotImplementedError("read-only")

findings.suggestion: Give the read-only case a type callers cannot receive where a writable Store is expected.

findings.title: legacy_export is not reached by any mapped flow
findings.rationale: Not reached by any of the 14 mapped flows — confirm before deleting. Tracing cannot see reflection, dependency injection or configuration-declared entry points.
findings.suggestion: Check for dynamic callers and configuration references, then decide.
